schema_note: five-vector: live (positive) + pre-expired (upper-bound negative) + act-binding-carrying live (positive, extra claim) + not-yet-valid (LOWER-bound negative, added 2026-07-29 at Tima's request) + cross-subject (positive, DIFFERENT sub, added 2026-08-05). verification_time is stamped PER VECTOR after minting, not copied from a pre-minting authored_at.
integrity_convention: Every vector carries token_len (character count of the compact JWT string) and token_sha256 (hex SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes) as FLAT fields — your field names, deliberately. We had built it as a nested fingerprint={chars,sha256}: same convention, zero interop, because it was announced in prose without naming the fields. Yours shipped across 27 vectors and ours had shipped in none, so ours moved. Check it before parsing anything: a mismatch means the token was altered between our send and your read, which is a different fault from a vector that is simply wrong. Introduced 2026-07-29 after a 24-Jun vector failed in your runner and it took a byte-comparison against our Sent copy to place the fault. Declaring this key makes the stamp MANDATORY in our verifier: an unstamped vector fails instead of skipping. Cross-week use: this week's -expired vector IS last week's -live token, so its token_sha256 must equal the one you recorded last week. That makes the rotation invariant something you can check rather than something I assert — and it must be checked over the SENT bytes, not the archive: our 17-Jun and 24-Jun seams are internally consistent inside our own corpus and broken on the wire, so an archive-only chain shows green across a hole.
lower_bound_convention: Every vector declares lower_bound_source: 'token.nbf' when the decoded payload carries an RFC 7519 §4.1.5 nbf claim, 'verifier_policy_on_iat' when it does not and the lower bound is therefore a verifier's own future-iat rule (§4.1.6 gives iat no validity boundary). Declaring this key makes the field MANDATORY in our verifier and asserted in BOTH directions: a vector claiming token.nbf whose payload has no nbf fails, and so does one still claiming verifier_policy_on_iat after the issuer starts emitting nbf. The sidecar notBefore must RESTATE that bound, never invent one — through drop #10 it silently restated iat, which is what let a 'lower-bound negative' be passed by reading the sidecar when production has no sidecar (your finding 1, 2026-08-12).

subject_pin.note: The conformance subject is PINNED to this account for every vector EXCEPT the one carrying subject_assert.must_differ_from_pinned. al_trust.level is a per-subject value (score+confidence, then capped by account tier and evidence-mix gates) and is NOT comparable across subjects — verifiers must not pin the level string for policy. Assertable, not just readable: fail the drop if any other vector's sub differs from this one.

predecessor.note: This drop's -expired vector IS that token, so its token_sha256 below must equal expected_live_token_sha256 here AND the value you recorded last week from the wire. Three independent places, one digest: ours at build time, ours in the vector, yours from last week's mail.

vectors.verifier_must: validate signature against pinned JWKS, then check BOTH window bounds at verification_time
reject at the window check at verification_time; signature validity does not rescue an expired token

act_binding.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JCS. Keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit at serialization time (NOT insertion order); string-only values, NO Unicode normalization (RFC 8785 3.1: strings preserved as is - we normalized NFC through 2026-08-05 and removed it); no whitespace. For this preimage the sort yields action < goal < target. digest = 'sha256:' + base64url(SHA-256(utf8(JCS(preimage)))).

vectors.verifier_must: validate signature against pinned JWKS and check the window at verification_time (positive vector, same as live); THEN decode urn:dashclaw:act-binding, recompute the digest over the JCS canonicalization of the preimage, and confirm it equals the claim hash byte-for-byte. The act-binding claim is an EXTRA claim: it neither rescues nor sinks window/signature validity.

vectors.vector_note: Same token bytes as aat-2026-08-19-live: ONLY verification_time differs (lower bound minus 3600s). Shared bytes deliberate (agreed 2026-07-29). HONEST LIMIT unchanged from drop 10: no nbf claim, bound under test is a verifier future-iat rule. Replay: run with replay state RESET OR ISOLATED; a shared stateful verifier treating jti as one-time-use correctly rejects at jti_check.
vectors.verifier_must: reject at the window check at verification_time because verification_time < notBefore; a valid signature does not rescue a token that is not yet valid

vectors.vector_note: DELIBERATE cross-subject vector. CLAIM WITHDRAWN 2026-08-12 (Tima, finding 3): same-policy-decision-is-the-bug does not follow; replaced by the two settleable invariants.
vectors.verifier_must: validate signature against the pinned JWKS and check both window bounds at verification_time (positive vector, same as live); THEN assert sub != subject_pin.sub, and assert: (1) a consumer must not substitute the pinned subject al_trust when this subject has none, and (2) it must not throw on the absent field.
